messages:
maria: FYI we've got a Priority 2 from Acme: p95/p99 for tool/function-calls shot up after yesterday's runtime rollout. Customer reports their router->tool latency goes from ~80ms to 400-800ms intermittently. Posting stack traces and repro below. @kevin @sam-eng can you take a look?

kevin: On it. Can you paste the exact request and any headers (schema validation flag, model id, routing tags)?

maria: Repro curl (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/call_tool \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rw-instruct-3b","input":"do x","tool":"search","structured_output":true,"validate_schema":true}'
```
Observed timings (customer traces):
- client -> our edge: 20-30ms
- edge auth + router: 10-20ms
- router -> model runtime: 60-100ms (baseline) BUT: when structured_output + validate_schema=true, router waits 250-700ms extra before returning to client

jess: Do they have large schemas? Validation could be CPU bound on router or in a separate validation service. Any logs with "schema-validator"?

maria: They supplied a ~18KB JSON Schema with lots of nested "oneOf" rules. We grabbed trace where the router adds ~450ms. Attached log snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T10:12:33Z] router-id=rt-04 request=abc123 route=tool-router model=rw-instruct-3b flags=[structured_output,validate_schema] event=enter-validation
[2026-03-15T10:12:33Z] schema-validator pid=7123 start
[2026-03-15T10:12:33Z] schema-validator pid=7123 completed duration_ms=462 validation_result=pass
[2026-03-15T10:12:34Z] router-id=rt-04 event=forward-to-runtime duration_ms=12
```
So most of the extra time is in the schema validation step.

sam-eng: That matches the canary: yesterday we rolled a new schema-validator binary into router process (to reduce RPCs) which uses a new recursive walker. It improved small schemas but can regress on pathological nested schemas. Canary was small so it slipped through.

anita-ml: Could the validator be single-threaded and blocking the event loop? If it's in-process, it could increase tail latencies under concurrency.

kevin: Confirmed: the binary we shipped runs validation synchronously in router worker thread. Prior behavior was async RPC to a pool of validators (cpu-isolated). Canary merged an optimization that inlines validation to avoid RPC overhead for tiny schemas but didn't gate by schema size.

maria: Customer wants mitigations asap. Ideas?

jess: Short term: revert the canary or flip feature flag. We have a runtime flag to disable in-process validation and fall back to async pool.

ops: Rolling flag now to disable inline validation for all edge routers. ETA 6m. I'll post rollback steps if anything fails. :wrench:

deploy-bot: deploy started by ops: disable-inline-schema-validation -> 3 clusters -> 12 nodes

kevin: Also propose a per-request guard: if schema size > 4KB or recursion depth > X, punt to async pool. We'll add heuristics and a telemetry counter.

anita-ml: For customers with high structured-output usage, we can suggest: 1) pre-compile schema on upload (we already store parsed form), 2) use validate_schema=false and do validation offline with a webhook, or 3) if they control schemas, reduce use of deep oneOf chains.

maria: Customer OK w/ temporary workaround. They asked if we can provide an SLA note or mitigation guide. I'll send a postmortem note after this.

ops: Flag rolled out. Observing p95 drop on the affected tenant from ~680ms to ~120ms within 2m.

kevin: I'll open a follow-up with the runtime team to: 1) add schema-size heuristic (in-process only for < 2KB), 2) async pool auto-scaling for spikes, 3) add sampling of heavy schemas to infra for analysis.

jess: Also add a fallback: if validation takes >200ms, cancel inline validation and fallback to async with a logged reason tag so we can attribute cost.

maria: Customer reply: "Thanks — latency looks back to normal, will test more tomorrow. Can you share a timeline and whether this is tenant-specific?"

kevin: Timeline: immediate mitigation done (flag). Short-term patch (heuristics + timeout) ETA 48h. Long-term refactor (safe inline path + compiled validators) target 3 weeks. Not tenant-specific but only shows up for tenants with large/complex schemas and high QPS.

anita-ml: Suggest adding a mitigation doc in support KB: "Structured output validation and latency — when to disable validate_schema". I'll draft it.

maria: Sounds good. I'll reply to customer with the mitigation and the 48h patch ETA, and attach suggested temporary configs (validate_schema=false or route to dedicated pool).

ops: FYI we've created monitoring alerts: schema-validation-duration.p99 > 250ms -> paged to eng-runtime.

kevin: Opening internal ticket RW-1428 to track fixes and postmortem. Assigning to eng-runtime and eng-sre.

maria: Thanks team. Closing the escalation once customer confirms stable. :pray:
